_comment: A SONAME that names a slot rather than a project -> how to tell which project
is filling it.
Read by identify-elf-presence.py. elf-soname-map.json deliberately leaves
`libc` out, because the name says only that something is the C library and not
which one. The corpus shows why that matters: three different projects fill
that slot across seven vendor images, and their licences differ — musl is MIT,
glibc is LGPL, uClibc is LGPL. A notice that says `libc` has not answered the
question a notice exists to answer.
The library names itself inside the file. musl writes `musl libc` into its
loader banner and glibc writes `GNU C Library`, so the file settles what the
SONAME could not.
Why this is not the string search identify-elf-presence.py refuses to do. That
objection is about an unanchored search: `readline` in busybox's help text is
not evidence readline is linked in, because nothing tied the word to a role.
Here the structure has already picked the file — this ELF is the C library, by
its SONAME — and the string only chooses among a closed list of candidates for
that one slot. Structure names the slot; the string names the occupant. Only a
SONAME listed here is ever read this way, and only that file is read.
Rules for adding entries:
- Add a SONAME only when it genuinely names a slot. `libc` qualifies;
`libnetsnmp` does not, and belongs in elf-soname-map.json.
- Every marker must be one the project writes about itself, seen in a real
image, and recorded in `where`.
- Nothing is reported unless exactly one candidate matches. Two markers in
one file mean the file is not what we thought, and zero means the slot is
filled by something not listed. Both are ambiguity, and ambiguity is
reported as nothing rather than as a guess.
- Presence only. No version, no purl, no CPE, same as every other judgement
this script emits. musl's own version is in its file as a bare `1.1.6` with
nothing anchoring it — reading that would need the open pattern the
version-string table exists to avoid.
uClibc is deliberately absent. It names its shared object after its upstream
version (libuClibc-0.9.28.so), which version-string-map.json already reads, and
the marker would not settle the identity anyway: uclibc:uclibc ended at 0.9.33
and uclibc-ng_project:uclibc-ng picks up at 1.0, both writing `uClibc`. Adding
it would trade a correct answer for an ambiguous one.

libc.why: The C library slot. Filled by musl on MikroTik RouterOS and Ubiquiti UniFi, by glibc on D-Link, and by uClibc on Zyxel and NETGEAR (read from the filename instead, see above).

candidates.name: musl
candidates.where: MikroTik RouterOS lib/libc.so: `musl libc`; Ubiquiti UniFi AP AC Pro libc.so: `musl libc (mips-sf)`

candidates.name: glibc
candidates.where: D-Link DIR-X1560, its libc: `GNU C Library`
